blocks.content: Here's how a tunneling fallback would look across the two components — full write-up in [Tunneling fallback design sketch](intent://local/loopback-rewrite/note/abfd1c9f-4fd5-4ffc-bba8-ac81bc83db41), now linked from the spec's non-goals.

flowchart LR B[Embedded browser] -->|"http://127.0.0.1:localPort"| T[Electron main - TunnelManager
net.createServer per port] T -->|"binary stream frames over wss://daemon/tunnel
(same bearer token)"| D[intentd tunnel route] D -->|"TcpStream to 127.0.0.1:remotePort
(daemon loopback only)"| S[Dev server on daemon host]

**Rust (intentd)** — a new `/tunnel` WS route beside the JSON-RPC endpoint, same bearer-token auth but **binary frames**, speaking a tiny mux: `[opcode][streamId u32][payload]` with `OPEN(port)/OPEN_OK/OPEN_ERR/DATA/EOF/CLOSE` (WS message boundaries make this ~6 opcodes; no need for yamux). Each `OPEN` does `TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port))` and runs two copy tasks with bounded channels for backpressure. Policy: daemon-loopback targets only, stream caps, agent/workspace attribution, idle timeouts.

**Electron (FE main)** — a `TunnelManager` that lazily opens the single tunnel WS (reusing the existing transport's URL/token/cert pinning), and `forwardPort(remotePort) → localPort` via `net.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:0`, piping each accepted socket to a stream (`socket.pause/resume` against `ws.bufferedAmount`).

**Why it's the right fallback shape:**
- It slots behind the work already in flight: rewrite + probe first; **probe fails → `forwardPort()` and navigate to `127.0.0.1:localPort`** instead, result echoing `tunneled: true`. The model's URL convention doesn't change at all.
- Raw TCP forwarding transparently carries WebSockets/HMR/SSE — an HTTP request/response proxy over JSON-RPC (the obvious simpler alternative) would break dev-server hot reload and stream bodies.
- It fixes exactly the cases rewrite can't: servers bound to `127.0.0.1` on the daemon, firewalled ports — with zero daemon-network exposure, and the browser's `Host` header stays loopback (so Vite-style `allowedHosts` checks pass, which hostname rewrite can trip).

**Protocol impact**: a new PROTOCOL.md section (tunnel endpoint + frame format), so the intentd-first merge rule applies.

Meanwhile, the helper-task implementor is still running; I'll re-delegate the held tasks when it settles. Want me to turn the tunnel design into scheduled follow-up tasks now, or keep it parked until we see whether rewrite + probe covers real usage?
